conservation.condition_narrative:
- Paper is heavily cockled and wrinkled. 
- There are scattered slightly brown inclusions scattered throughout the paper 
- Shadows of hinges visible at top. 
- Scattered metallic inclusions throughout. 
- Thicker areas of paint have network cracking but are stable 
Frame is in very good condition with a minor abrasion on the left rail near the center.
conservation.report_notes: Information provided for *Access O'Keeffe* by Brooklyn Museum of Art in 2025.

materials.content:
Watercolor on very thin, beige, very smooth laid paper, Japanese gampi
(Source: Paper Survey researched by Judith C. Walsh and published in Lynes, 1999.)

cr_data.provenance: Until 1958 Downtown Gallery (The), New York, N.Y., then Purchased by Brooklyn Museum (The); provenance may be incomplete (Source: Brooklyn Museum of Art, 2025)
remarks_1999: Not recorded Whitney Archive. Abiquiú Notebooks after 1977 indicates, "Sold by Halpert, April 1958." Completed in Virginia before August move to Texas. Pictured in 1923 New York (Anderson) Stieglitz installation photograph, see Appendix III, figure 22. See cat. nos. 91, 93, 94. (Source: Lynes, 1999)

description: Two semicircular forms that fade from dark blue on the outside to green and gray at their centers sit in the middle of the composition. A few rectangular strips of blue paint extend diagonally across the bottom right of the image. The forms contrast with the exposed, plain white paper surrounding them.
